chapter: Later bands, Joe Turner and records
title: The one record he made with his sons
summary: A blues cut for WYLD that never got distributed.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Okay. You say you made one record. We were talking before about that.

Yeah, we made a blues with my two sons. We cut that W-Y-L-D, the color station. But then they broke it up. When they was cleaning up, they broke it. I'll replace it for you because I got boxed in the team.
And your two sons and you and who else?
Oh, and his heart and the same fella that I played with him quite often. We used to play together. Yeah.
Was it put out or was it sold by him?
No, no. He's right. Or the man that cut it, he couldn't make contact with A1 distributors. You ever heard of them?
He could not make no kind of contact with him. Mm-hmm. He cut it for Dr. Mighty.
He's some kind of record scout. Mm-hmm. And he never could make contact with A1 distributors.
Was it singing on it or was it playing?
Yeah, singing. Both sides. My son sang. Okay. Raymond.
